 Salmonella outbreak linked to raw oysters sold in Virginia, CDC says
 Prev 
 Next 
 WTKR Latest Headlines and Weather: Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026 
 By: 
 WTKR Web Staff
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 NORFOLK, Va. — A salmonella outbreak has been linked to raw oysters sold in Virginia, according to a notice from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). 
 The CDC report said the Little Wicomico Oyster Company voluntarily recalled oysters from the Little Wicomico River in Virginia and contacted its customers. 
 The whole (shellstock) oysters were harvested between Sept. 18, 2026 and Oct. 8, 2026. 
 In addition to Virginia and Maryland, CBS News reports the oysters were distributed to retailers in California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, North Carolina, New Jersey, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and Washington, D.C.
 So far, 27 people have contracted salmonella as a result. 
 The Little Wicomico River harvest area has been closed as a precaution.
 "Consumers, restaurants and retailers should not eat, sell, or serve recalled oysters from Little Wicomico Oyster Company harvested in the Little Wicomico River from September 18, through October 8, 2026, and should dispose of potentially contaminated products or contact their distributor to arrange for destruction," the CDC website states.
 The CDC advises anyone with the following symptoms to contact their doctor:
 Diarrhea and a fever higher than 102°F
 Diarrhea for more than 2 days that is not improving
 Bloody diarrhea
 So much vomiting that you cannot keep liquids down
 Signs of dehydration, such as:
 Not peeing much
 Dry mouth and throat
 Feeling dizzy when standing up
 This is a developing story, so check back with WTKR.com for updates. Email News 3 if you have info, photos or videos to share.
